artworks.title: The Fall of the Giants (Sistine Chapel)
artworks.description: On the altar wall of the Sistine Chapel, Michelangelo stages the Gigantomachy as naked colossi hurled from heaven by the wrath of Olympian gods — the visual tradition Apollodorus compresses into named duels at Phlegra, where Heracles the mortal ally was required before any Giant could fall.

artworks.title: The Gigantomachy (Pergamon Altar Frieze, detail)
artworks.description: The great Hellenistic altar at Pergamon celebrated cosmic order defended against earthborn violence; its Gigantomachy frieze — gods striding over serpent-footed giants — became the canonical image of the war Hesiod only names in the castration-blood brood and Apollodorus retells as the fullest surviving battle-list.
